OCTOBER 31: The Hanwha Eagles will be posting third baseman Si Hwan Roh for Major League teams this offseason, according to multiple reports out of South Korea (including Jeeho Yoo of Yonhap News).  The Eagles have asked the Korean Baseball Organization to post Roh, and the KBO League has subsequently told MLB teams about Roh’s availability. It isn’t clear if Roh’s 30-day posting window is now open, or if an official posting announcement will come in the next few days.  Once Roh is posted, he’ll have 30 days (shorter than the 45-day posting period for NPB players) to reach an agreement with a Major League team.  If a deal is reached, the Eagles will receive a posting fee worth 20% of the first $25MM of Roh’s contract, 17.5% of the next $25MM, and $15% for anything beyond $50MM. The timing of Roh’s posting is particularly noteworthy this offseason since the collective bargaining agreement expires on December 1, and a lockout is expected to follow.  If Roh and other KBO/NPB players posted this winter haven’t signed with a big league team by December 1, they’ll be caught up in the lockout transactions freeze just like their MLB counterparts.  In Roh’s case, the shorter 30-day window probably allows for a greater understanding of his market, as most or even all of his posting period (depending on when it begins) could be up by December 1. Should a posted player not find an acceptable deal before or after their window expires, he’ll return to his former club for the 2027 season.  There’s an added wrinkle in Roh’s situation, as he would be returning to the Eagles to begin an 11-year contract extension signed last February.  That extension begins with the 2027 season, though it included a provision that Roh will first be posted for MLB teams this offseason.  If Roh does indeed move to the majors, he is also contractually required to return to the Eagles whenever he should return to KBO upon the conclusion of his MLB tenure. The 11-year contract will pay Roh $30.7 billion won, or a little over $23MM as per the current conversion rate beween the won and the U.S. dollar.  With some significant financial security already lined up, Roh has some leverage in fielding offers from Major League teams, though an MLB club could conceivably offer him a lower sum than $23MM but in a shorter timeframe. The KBO League is generally considered to be a rung below Nippon Professional Baseball, and as such there is less of a track record of players (particularly hitters) making the successful transition from South Korea to the majors.  Roh’s market will hinge on how many big league clubs feel he has the tools to produce against higher-level pitching, though there’s some intrigue given how well Roh has hit in his home country. Another week of college football did not disappoint. Both Week 7 and Week 8 saw a lot of upsets, and while this weekend didn’t see as many — there was a lot of good football. The biggest upset of the weekend took place in Los Angeles.  USC took down the Buckeyes, who were without star quarterback Julian Sayin. Ohio State started freshman Luke Fahey in his place and the offense stalled too many times, not being able to sustain drives. USC was able to get out to a quick lead and never looked back. In other news, Indiana went into overtime for the second game in a row, and came away with a win for the second week in a row.  Following another great weekend of football, here is our weekly stock up, stock down.  MORE: Predicting College Football Playoff field after Week 9: Ohio State falls after stunning loss Iowa was coming off a tough loss on the road last weekend to Minnesota. The Hawkeyes’ offense couldn’t get rolling in the 13-10 loss they suffered to the Gophers. And Wisconsin was playing as good football as anyone, but it’s never easy to win in Kinnick.  The Badgers found that out during Iowa’s 30-0 win over Wisconsin in Week 9. Iowa’s win propels the Hawkeyes to 6-2, and Iowa is firmly in the hunt to make the College Football Playoff, with a outside chance of getting to the Big Ten Championship Game. Quarterback Hank Brown was great, throwing for 222 yards and two scores.  Iowa has to go on the road to both Northwestern and Illinois, while getting Purdue and Nebraska at home. The ‘Cats lost to Oregon this week, and Iowa’s road to 10-2 looks possible.  Major questions surrounded Ohio State after Julian Sayin exited the game two weeks ago against Indiana. The Buckeyes held on to beat the Hoosiers, but the moment looked too big for freshman Luke Fahey when he came into the game. To his credit, Fahey played respectably for his first career start on Saturday against USC. He made freshman mistakes, but his playmakers also dropped some passes in the game. Fahey’s offensive line didn’t do him any favors, either. The USC defense had push off the ball and Fahey faced a lot of pressure.   The Buckeyes lost, 30-18, and Ohio State dropped to 6-2 on the season. And for the Buckeyes, they actually ran the ball quite well for how their run game has been in 2026. The problem was Ohio State’s defense.  USC had a few big plays en route to the win and Ohio State isn’t built to counter that. Without Sayin behind center, the Buckeyes are going to need to keep things close, or get out to an early lead. With games against Oregon, Northwestern, Nebraska, and Michigan still to be played, the Buckeyes are no longer guaranteed to make the playoff.  The defending national champions appear to be very beatable. But the only stat that matters — wins and losses — the Hoosiers are 8-1. Indiana got past Minnesota in overtime in Week 9 and won 23-16. It was the Hoosiers’ second overtime game in as many weeks.  In all reality, Indiana could have four losses in a row. Nebraska could’ve beaten the Hoosiers, Ohio State did beat Indiana, and both Michigan and Minnesota had chances to win the game. But that’s all shoulda, coulda, woulda. Curt Cignetti’s team continues to find a way to win games.  In a league full of parity, nobody is going to judge Indiana’s wins, or how the Hoosiers get them. All that matters is that Indiana continues to win, and that’s what it’s doing. Grant Wilson took over for Josh Hoover in the game and he passed for 156 yards and a score. That will be something to keep an eye on when Indiana takes the field in two weeks against USC. This was in Lubbock, but Arizona has been the better team. Texas Tech was coming off a loss to Cincinnati last week, and the Red Raiders opted to make a quarterback change ahead of the top-25 showdown. Former Boston College and Florida State transfer Thomas Castellanos started in place of Will Hammond, and he had three total touchdowns.  Arizona was up 17-7 and then 23-17 toward the end of the third quarter. But Texas Tech’s newfound offense was too much for the Wildcats’ defense. Plus, Arizona quarterback Noah Fifita made some uncharacteristic mistakes while throwing for over 400 yards.  After losing 34-26 to Texas Tech, Arizona fell to 6-2 (3-2). The Wildcats have now lost to both BYU and the Red Raiders. Their path to the Big 12 title game is sparse. The Big 12 might only get one team into the College Football Playoff — two at most — and Arizona might’ve lost its spot.  Week 10 is going to showcase one of the biggest games of the season when Miami travels to Notre Dame to take on the Irish. With that game taking place next weekend, both programs faced some adveristy in a look-ahead game.  Navy gashed Notre Dame early on and the Irish were up just 14-13 at half. But Marcus Freeman’s team put it on in the second half and came away with a 35-13 win over Navy.  It wasn’t the same for Miami. The Hurricanes took on more than they wanted against North Carolina. The Tar Heels continue to improve under Bill Belichick and North Carolina was right in the game until the final whistle blew. Miami would pull away with a 38-35 win.  Now all eyes turn to Week 10.  Remember Florida’s 52-28 win over then-No. 4 Ole Miss? Seems like an eternity ago. The Gators would lose their next two games before stunning Texas on the road. But Florida met its match on Saturday in Atlanta against Georgia.  The Bulldogs beat Florida 27-8, and the scoreboard doesn’t match how the game went. Georgia dominated from start to finish, and the Gators’ offense had no idea how to get things going. Starting quarterback Aaron Philo was benched after he threw an interception. Tramell Jones Jr. tried to spark Florida’s offense, but he tossed two interceptions and lost a fumble. Star running back Jadan Baugh could only muster 38 yards on 17 carries. UF’s top-five offense in the SEC looked more like a bottom-tier offense. The Gators fell to 5-3 on the season, and while we’ve seen a lot of good from Jon Sumrall in Year 1, Florida is clearly a year away.  — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —  Vikings coach sends message after Lions’ Jack Campbell suffers scary injury Live stream Commanders vs Eagles for free: Watch NFL SNF, TV channel Frustrated Jerry Jones makes Brian Schottenheimer’s job status clear Ravens’ coach shares devastating Lamar Jackson injury news after Bills loss Vikings doomed by late decision to just give away football to Lions Florida State fires Mike Norvell after Saturday’s Clemson loss Lions LB Jack Campbell stretchered off field after scary injury vs. Vikings Eastern Conference team reportedly in trade talks for Red Wings’ Dylan Larkin How to watch Patriots vs Dolphins: NFL, live stream, TV channel, start time How to watch Chiefs vs Broncos: NFL, live stream, TV channel, start time © 2025 TheBigLead – All Rights Reserved

The proposal could help market infrastructure institutions (MIIs) make greater commercial use of their existing infrastructure and capabilities, while reducing the approval burden for activities that directly support market operations. The regulator last week proposed an automatic approval route for specified activities related or incidental to an MII's core functions. These include activities undertaken at the regulator's direction, certain transfers of shares between an MII and its subsidiaries, and deployment of funds by an operating subsidiary exclusively from earnings generated through its own operations. “Think market data and analytics, technology and information services, intra-group share transfers, or a subsidiary reinvesting its own operating earnings (route A),” said Nikunj Saraf, CEO of Choice Wealth. “The operational gain is real: shorter time-to-market, board-level accountability replacing central pre-clearance, and the ability to monetise the deep data and infrastructure these institutions already own,” he said. The proposal also covers certain activities undertaken through investee companies regulated by other financial-sector regulators, where SEBI has previously approved the activity and its scope remains unchanged. However, while governance conditions are principally outlined by SEBI, the details will need to be worked out by the MII’s governing board. The boards will have to balance between specifics and allow flexibility to subsidiaries but within limits, Vanya Singh, Partner at Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas said. "The relaxation could enable MIIs to respond more efficiently to evolving market requirements, optimise capital deployment and pursue operational synergies," said Hardeep Sachdeva, senior partner at AZB & Partners. The proposed flexibility, however, would need to be balanced against the risk of commercial interests interfering with the regulatory responsibilities of exchanges and depositories. The MII’s governing board would have to approve each new activity or fund deployment and ensure that it does not create conflicts with the institution’s market functions or compromise resources needed for technology upgrades, regulatory obligations and investor protection. The proposal also requires safeguards such as arm’s-length arrangements, ring-fencing of shared resources, fit-and-proper compliance and half-yearly reporting to SEBI. “The possibility of conflicts of interest constitutes perhaps the most consequential consideration arising from the proposed framework,” said Tushar Kumar, Advocate, Supreme Court of India. “Financial safeguards alone cannot adequately address conflicts arising from preferential access, information asymmetry or competing institutional incentives.” Burzin Bharucha, Partner at White & Brief, said the framework would need clear separation between an MII’s commercial and regulatory functions, with SEBI retaining the ability to intervene where market integrity or investor protection is at risk. The proposed automatic route will not extend to recognised clearing corporations. Activities outside the specified categories would continue to require prior SEBI approval. Chad Lowe and his wife, Kim Painter, have put their Los Angeles home on the market after the untimely death of their 13-year-old daughter, Fiona. Lowe, 58, and Painter, 52, recently put their four-bedroom house up for sale, according to real estate records viewed by Us on Saturday, October 31. The couple accepted an offer for $3.249 million, contingent on certain conditions being met. (TMZ was first to report the news.) Lowe and Painter, who purchased the property in March 2025 months after losing their house in the devastating Palisades wildfires, have not publicly addressed the real estate move. Us has reached out for comment. One month earlier, Lowe and Painter announced that their 13-year-old daughter had died by suicide. (They also share daughters Mabel, 17, and Nixie, 10.) “We are deeply heartbroken by the loss of our beloved Fiona,” Lowe and Painter wrote in a September statement, remembering Fiona as “a loving young girl who was smart, creative and loved to dance.” They continued at the time, “She was adored by her sisters and she was deeply loved by her parents. In fact, she was the light of our lives. Her passing is devastating for our entire family and we ask for prayers and privacy at this time. If you or someone you know is struggling with mental health, please reach out to the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline by calling or texting 988.” Fiona’s older sister, Mabel, has also been candid about grieving the death of her sibling. “I love you so much, Fiona ❤️. I wish your short time here was easier and I hope your mind is at ease now,” she wrote via Instagram on October 3. “I will honor you forever and keep your memory alive. I love you, I hope you knew just how much.” Lowe, for his part, returned to social media days later to repost a poignant message about grief and healing. You have successfully subscribed.
